info.bio:
The La's eran una banda de Liverpool de finales de los 80 y principios de los 90, liderada por Lee Mavers (voz) y John Power (bajo y coros). Su mayor éxito fue "There She Goes".

Se formaron en 1983. Mike Badger, miembro fundador del grupo, afirmaba que el nombre de la banda se le ocurrió en un sueño. Lee Mavers se unió al grupo en 1984, en principio como guitarra rítmica, pero poco a poco se convirtió en el compositor de la banda, y posteriormente en el líder de la misma.

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: Costly and Unhappy Album Release (1990)
podcast.body: After 12 studio sessions, 10 band members, 7 producers, and over £1 million in studio costs, the band was forced to release their record on October 1st, 1990, despite Mavers' profound dissatisfaction with the outcome. He was quoted saying, "I hate it. There was not one good thing I could find to say about it. It's like a snake with a broken back." "Eventually, after 12 studio sessions, 10 band members, seven producers, and over 1 million pounds in studio costs, he was forced to release the record on October 1st, 1990, even though he still wasn't happy with what had been recorded. In fact, he was quoted as saying, I hate it. There was not one good thing I could find to say about it. It's like a snake with a broken back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stressful Album Recording (1990)
podcast.body: The recording of their sole album was incredibly stressful, largely due to Lee Mavers' "insane perfectionism" and his struggle to capture the exact sound he envisioned onto tape. "Recording that one album was incredibly stressful, compounded by Mayvers' insane perfectionism, and an inability to get down on tape exactly what he heard in his head."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Limited Post-1991 Public Appearances
podcast.body: Lee Mavers has appeared in concert 20 times since 1991 and is rumored to communicate with other musicians like William Gallagher and Paul Weller, despite his general reclusiveness. "Lee has appeared in concert 20 times since 1991. He's rumored to talk to other musicians from time to time. William Gallagher is rumored to be a mate, so was Paul Weller."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "60s Dust" Anecdote
podcast.body: An apocryphal story suggests that Lee Mavers once located what he called "60's dust," allegedly sound dust from the 1960s, which he sprinkled on his instruments before playing. "An apocryphal story, well probably apocryphal, says that Mayvers somehow located what he called 60's dust, which is just like it's sound dust allegedly from the 1960's, and he sprinkled it on his instruments before he started playing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "A Secret Liverpool in Search of The La's" Book
podcast.body: A book titled "A Secret Liverpool in Search of The La's" was written, reflecting the persistent mystery surrounding the band and its frontman. "There was even a book called A Secret Liverpool in Search of The Lies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bandmate Paranoia
podcast.body: Bandmates grew paranoid about their ability to play because they could never achieve what Mavers demanded of them. "Bandmates grew paranoid about their ability to play because they could never do what Mayvers asked them to do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Current Life and Income
podcast.body: As far as is known, Mavers resides in a Liverpool suburb as a family man, stubbornly refusing to speak with most journalists or engage with the music industry. He financially sustains his family through the licensing and repeated coverage of the band's single hit, which earns him a regular six-figure income year after year. "As far as we know, Mavers is living in a Liverpool suburb as a family man, stubbornly unwilling to talk to most every journalist or engage in anything to do with the vile music industry. He is pretty much completely unknowable. So how does he and his family make ends meet? With this one hit Wonder Hit, which has been licensed and covered over and over again through the last three plus decades, burning him a regular six-figure income year after year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lee Mavers' Disappearance and Rumors
podcast.body: Following the album's release, Lee Mavers disappeared, leading to various rumors: that he became a painter, went into home decor, became a hopeless heroin addict (though he later recovered), was ceaselessly re-recording old songs, or was living in a monastery where monks praised his musical genius. "And with that, he disappeared. Oh, there were rumors and stories. He'd become a painter, he'd got into home decor, he'd become a hopeless heroin addict. He was re-recording and re-recording songs from that album in a Sisyphean attempt to get them right, that he was living in a monastery, where the resident monks had declared him to be the best thing to happen in music since Mozart."
